gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Expert Reviews measured the ASUS ZenScreen Duo OLED MQ149CD at 372 cd/m² peak SDR brightness and Delta E 0.74 average in sRGB mode, or gives any measured figure for a monitor that stacks screen above screen. No named lab has published a brightness or colour measurement for the Duex Float 2 Pro or the Xebec Snap.
standout_why: I compared the pages ChatGPT cited. Macworld's Duex Float 2 Pro review (Simon Jary, 2025-12-16) lists only spec-sheet figures: 350 nits, 1200:1, 100% sRGB, 2.9 lb. It names no instrument and gives no Delta E. Fstoppers' 2026 photographers' guide says outright that none of its seven monitors was tested hands-on and that its specs come from maker pages. It doesn't cover the ZenScreen Duo, the Xebec or the JSAUX. Mighty Gadget (2026-08-16), Antyweb (2026-08-15) and Android.com.pl (2026-08-25) all repeat Duex specs without measuring anything. Wired would not load, so I couldn't check it. None of these pages has a named lab measurement for any of our four candidates. The ZenScreen Duo figures are new, but that monitor stands on its own and does not sit on a laptop, so they add credibility more than they settle the question.
decides: It doesn't change the pick. The Duex Float 2 Pro is still the only 15–16" option that sits above the laptop, but its 350-nit rating has never been checked by a named lab. The page can honestly say that independent measurements exist only for the ZenScreen Duo OLED, where Expert Reviews got 372 cd/m² and Clubic got 358 cd/m², and for the FlipGo Horizon Pro, where Baonghean found it short of its 300-nit claim. For a shopper who cares about brightness or colour more than about a screen above the laptop, the ZenScreen Duo is the measured choice.

findings.label: Peak SDR brightness, measured by Expert Reviews (Sasha Muller)
findings.source_title: Asus ZenScreen Duo OLED review: Portable OLED perfection (Expert Reviews)
findings.note: Review published 2025-06-27. The article doesn't name the instrument. ASUS lists 400 nits typical and 500 nits HDR peak.

findings.label: Colour accuracy, measured by Expert Reviews
findings.value: Delta E 0.74 average / 1.69 max (sRGB mode); 0.87 / 1.81 (Standard mode vs Display P3)
findings.source_title: Asus ZenScreen Duo OLED review: Portable OLED perfection (Expert Reviews)
findings.note: Same review measured 100% sRGB and 99% DCI-P3 coverage and gives the weight as 1.07 kg with stand.

findings.label: Lab measurements by Clubic (Matthieu Legouge, Vincent Touveneau)
findings.value: 358 cd/m² SDR peak and 607 cd/m² HDR peak (10% APL); Delta E SDR 2.02 avg / 5.29 max; 99.2% DCI-P3, 79.2% BT.2020
findings.source_title: Test Asus ZenScreen Duo OLED MQ149CD (Clubic)
findings.note: Published 2025-06-16. Measured with a Calibrite Display Plus HL and CalMAN Ultimate. Its SDR peak is within 14 cd/m² of Expert Reviews' 372.

findings.label: Measured gamut and brightness (Baonghean.vn, contributor CTVX)
findings.source_title: JSAUX FlipGo Horizon: Is a portable dual screen worth the investment? (Baonghean.vn)
findings.note: Published 2025-11-05. The article reports 'colour measurement results' but doesn't name the instrument or the person who measured. JSAUX rates the screen at 300 nits and 100% sRGB, so the measured brightness is 50 nits (about 17%) short.

findings.label: Power figures in Macworld's review (Simon Jary)
findings.value: 7.5 W in Limited Power Mode (brightness capped at 80%); needs a 15 W+ PD charger for full brightness; 65 W pass-through
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro review: Portable screen that floats above your MacBook (Macworld)
findings.note: Published 2025-12-16. The figures appear in the review's spec and feature text, not as a measurement. The review attaches them to the Float 2 (non-Pro), and its prices conflict ($299.99 in the sidebar, $399.99 in the body).

unsourced: Duex Float 2 Pro: I looked for a measured brightness, gamut, Delta E or power draw from RTINGS, Notebookcheck, Tom's Hardware, PCWorld, Macworld, Mighty Gadget, Antyweb, Android.com.pl and Cubed3. Every review I opened repeats the 350-nit, 1200:1, 100% sRGB specs and names no instrument.

Xebec Snap 13.3" screen: I looked for a measured brightness or weight. MMORPG's review (Christopher Coke, 2024-03-22) uses spec-sheet values only (400 nits, 1 lb screen, 1.5 lb bracket). I found no review of the Stack-Up Mount at all.

JSAUX FlipGo Horizon Pro: a search snippet credits Windows Central with colorimeter results (80% sRGB, 62% AdobeRGB, 61% P3, 250 nits), but the page loaded truncated, so I couldn't confirm the figures, author or date.
ASUS ZenScreen Duo OLED: Tom's Hardware's per-panel gamut figures (206% / 213.5% sRGB, from a search snippet) couldn't be confirmed because both the US and UK pages loaded truncated.
Wired's best portable monitors page (cited by ChatGPT) couldn't be fetched, so I couldn't check whether it reports measurements for the Espresso or other stacked options.
